body:
I reviewed head b90c310 against dev, including the adjacent probe and editor-layout code. The current fast checks, full tests, preview, and Codecov checks are green. I found three browser-side correctness issues that I would address before merge; the inline comments include the failure mode and a suggested direction.

Maintainability and structure:

- ProbeProj.re is now 2,544 lines and owns persisted projector state, mutable global display settings, sample caches, navigation/focus, menus and listeners, rich-renderer selection, and drawer rendering. Those are useful seams for ProbeSettings, ProbeNavigation, ProbeSampleMenu, ProbeRichView, and ProbeDrawer modules, leaving the projector implementation mostly as orchestration.
- ProbePerform.re is 1,424 lines and similarly combines target discovery, automatic-probe reconciliation, manual/multi-probe lifecycle, collision cleanup, focus, and step-into behavior. ProbeTargets, AutoProbePerform, and ProbeFocus would make the invariants and tests much easier to isolate.
- CardTypes/CardSyntax/CardView and MenuListener are good extractions in this branch; I would continue that pattern. In particular, ProbeProj.vacuous_value currently knows about CardSyntax to decide whether automatic rich rendering has evidence. That policy belongs on the RichProbe renderer interface as an auto-applicability/evidence predicate, so future list-shaped renderers do not add more domain checks to the generic probe module.
- ProbeStagger, RefractorShift, ScrollWidth, SampleAnchor, and FocusEffect are individually small, but together form a global mutable after-display subsystem. An editor-scoped layout-effects coordinator would give these caches an explicit owner and directly prevent the first two findings below.

Naming and comments:

- Settings.s and Settings.go hide whether code is reading state or dispatching an update; current and update/dispatch would be clearer, ideally behind a non-global interface.
- The strongest comments explain invariants, such as raw versus finalized sample maps, observation-span delegation, and agreement between reserved and measured drawer rows. Keep those close to the code.
- The long design-history comments are less durable. ProbeStagger links an implementation plan, AutoProbe describes Caret only as a top-level definition even though bare expressions are supported, and the RichProbe module comment ends mid-thought. I would trim these to current behavioral contracts and move the exegesis/history to maintained design docs.
- git diff --check reports trailing whitespace in hazel-programs/docs/reference/cards.hz on lines 8 and 38.

Overall, the card/view and listener extractions are heading in a good direction, but the new layout code needs editor identity to be a first-class input rather than relying on document-global selectors and refs.
